The lines and spaces of the staff are notations for specific intervals of pitch -- the vertical distance between lines and spaces indicate higher or lower pitch values, with the top line being the highest note and the bottom line being the lowest note.  In general the higher up you move on the staff, the higher in pitch the note will be, and moving right indicates a higher pitch as well.  The horizontal direction on the staff indicates rhythm values -- moving left indicates a slower rhythm and moving right indicates a faster rhythm.  Overall the lines and spaces of the staff map out a kind of sonic landscape for the musicians to navigate their way through.'
